title: Pro-étale realization
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a finite field $k_0$ of order $q$ and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with the coefficient categories and operations specified below; the assertion concerns its concrete pro-etale realizations, with the projection transformation constructed from the supplied operation and comparison data [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf].

Let $\Lambda$ be one of $A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ be pro-etale realizations of bounded constructible finite-Tor objects [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with the following meanings at the respective coefficient stages.

At a finite stage use the ordinary small pro-etale constant-$A_{E,n}$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The inputs may be presented with etale-origin witnesses $(K_0,e_K)$, $(L_0,e_L)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], where $K_0,L_0$ are bounded constructible etale complexes of finite Tor amplitude and $e_K:\nu_X^*K_0\cong K$, $e_L:\nu_Y^*L_0\cong L$; alternatively they may be given intrinsically as bounded constructible pro-etale complexes of finite Tor amplitude [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin, lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]. At the integral stage use the completed coefficient sheaf and the derived-complete constructible category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], with uniform finite Tor amplitude of the finite reductions as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Here realization and operations are the coherent finite-level constructions of the datum; tensor and pullback are completed. At $E$ use its rationalized integral category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the common finite-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

For a chosen compactification $c=(j,r)$ of $f$, the finite-stage projection component is the canonical proper counit-defined projection map followed by the open tensor comparison of [def-exchange-projection], with $Rf_!^c=Rr_*j_!$. Use the specified operation/comparison data of the datum to form its completed integral, rationalized, and common-stage components and the compactification comparisons intertwining these components. Thus $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ has type
$$
Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr),
$$
with the completed interpretation of the integral symbols. Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism in the indicated pro-etale coefficient category. The finite-stage assertion applies both to the explicit-witness and the intrinsic presentations of the inputs.

proof.text: At a finite stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, choose bounded constructible etale representatives $K_0,L_0$ and witnesses $e_K:A_XK_0\cong K$, $e_L:A_YL_0\cong L$, with $A_T=\nu_T^*$. The retained pair is precisely [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. If the objects are given intrinsically, the bounded-complex equivalence of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies these representatives. Apply [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] to each representative and its witness: the finite Tor bounds of $K,L$ give the same finite Tor bounds on $K_0,L_0$. Thus the etale projection formula's finite-Tor hypothesis on $L_0$ is available; bounded constructibility alone is not being used to infer it.

Choose the compactification $c=(j,p)$ used to form the projection morphism in [def-sf-pf, def-exchange-projection], so $f=pj$, with $p$ proper and $j$ an open immersion. This choice is part of the operation datum; no new compactification assertion is needed. Put $M_0=j_!K_0$ and $P_0=M_0\otimes^L p^*L_0$. Exactness of etale $j_!$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $M_0$ bounded, say in $[r,s]$. To check the bounded-below hypothesis required by the direct-image comparison, choose a bounded flat model of $L_0$ in its Tor interval $[a,b]$ by [lem-sf-etale-flat-model]. This bounded complex of flat sheaves is K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1). The canonical ringed pullback takes this K-flat model to a K-flat complex of flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], still supported in $[a,b]$, representing $p^*L_0$. Tensor it with a bounded representative of $M_0$ in $[r,s]$; the direct-sum total tensor has no terms outside $[r+a,s+b]$. By [def-kun-derived-tensor] it computes $P_0$. In particular both $M_0$ and $P_0$ are bounded below. The sites are taken small in the common larger universe. Properness supplies finite type and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separatedness implies quasi-separatedness [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus $p$ satisfies both morphism hypotheses of the comparison lemma.

Use the ringed-topos square with horizontal arrows $p_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and vertical arrows $\nu_{\overline X},\nu_Y$. Its constant-ring identifications and exact derived comparison are [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]; its pullback commutation is the inverse of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The exchange mate is $b_C$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]: its transpose is exactly $A_{\overline X}(\varepsilon_C)$ preceded by that inverse commutation. Thus these are the specified maps, with the same normalization. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] at $(M_0,L_0)$. Its two-composite equality gives the commutative square comparing the etale and pro-etale proper projection maps; it requires no Cartesian scheme square. The vertical tensor identifications are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The maps $b_{M_0},b_{P_0}$ are invertible by the canonical-mate lemma, since step 2 verified qcqs and bounded-below hypotheses.

Apply [lem-sf-comparison-open-tensor-coherence] to $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $K_0$, and $N=p_{\mathrm{et}}^*L_0$. Its displayed equality identifies the two routes from comparison of the etale open tensor factor to the pro-etale open tensor factor, including the canonical open-extension comparison $e$ and tensor and restriction comparisons. These are exactly the factors of the compactification-relative projection composite [def-exchange-projection]. Its hypotheses hold because the coefficient ring is finite and $j$ is open; it imposes no additional bounds. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] for $p$ identifies the second input with $p_{\mathrm{proet}}^*A_YL_0$, and its composition compatibility identifies the restriction to $X$ with $f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*A_YL_0$.

Postcompose the proper projection square of step 3 by $Rp_*$ of the open tensor factors of step 4. The equality in step 4 makes the resulting outer square commute: replace its open-factor composite by the equal opposite route, and then use the equality in step 3. By the formula $\operatorname{PF}^c=Rp_*(\gamma)\circ\pi_p$ in [def-exchange-projection], its horizontal arrows are precisely the compactification-relative projection maps. All its vertical arrows are composites of the invertible comparison arrows already identified in steps 3 and 4. This gives the required comparison of the actual projection composites.

The etale compact-support projection map at $(K_0,L_0)$ is invertible by the etale assertion of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], which requires a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes and precisely the bounded constructibility and Tor hypotheses verified in steps 1 and 2. On separated $k$-schemes this is also the statement of [thm-sf-pf-finite]. The more general lemma avoids imposing separatedness of $X$ and $Y$, which is not part of the operation datum. Only its etale assertion is used here; its pro-etale conclusion is not used to bypass the comparison argument. Apply the comparison functor $A_Y$ to its inverse. Its image is inverse to the image of the projection map by functoriality. The commuting square of step 5, whose vertical maps are invertible, expresses the pro-etale projection map at $(A_XK_0,A_YL_0)$ as this image conjugated by isomorphisms. It is therefore invertible. Finally use naturality of the specified projection transformation [def-exchange-projection] with respect to $e_K,e_L$ to conjugate this map to the one at $(K,L)$. This proves the finite-stage assertion for the compactification used to define the stated map.

Changing a finite-stage witness does not change this conclusion or the projection map it concerns. For two presentations $A_TF_0\cong F\cong A_TF_1$, full faithfulness on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] uniquely lifts the induced isomorphism $A_TF_0\cong A_TF_1$ to an isomorphism $F_0\cong F_1$; its inverse lifts as well, and their composites are identities by faithfulness. The comparison square and the open comparisons are natural in the inputs, so the two conjugations of step 6 give the same canonical projection component at $F$. This justifies the wording about supplied witnesses without treating the definition of a witness as an existence theorem. At the higher stages the word realization refers to the completed/rationalized/common-stage coefficient constructions, not the discrete finite-ring comparison.

source.place: Last sentence about witnesses; finite stages only

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, use the completed integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. An input in its finite-Tor subcategory has reductions $K_n,L_n$ with uniform cohomological and Tor bounds, by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; these are the finite-stage pro-etale objects already treated. Apply [thm-sf-pf-adic] directly on this pro-etale coefficient system: its conclusion is a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ realizing the compatible normalized finite-level projection maps. The map is the completed integral projection transformation of [def-sf-pf]. Thus the assertion at the integral stage follows on the stated domain. This uses the adic theorem's reconstruction and identification conclusion, rather than an unproved claim that a fixed discrete-coefficient $\nu^*$ handles completion or that conservativity detects equality of morphisms.

For $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] defines the rational category with the same objects as its integral category, so both inputs have integral representatives. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] makes every object a finite-stage pair and provides a common finite extension for the two inputs. There is no Karoubi completion at either stage. Their projection maps are the rationalized/common-stage maps specified in [def-sf-pf]. Apply [thm-sf-pf-field] to these representatives. Its conclusion gives the invertible projection maps over $E$ and over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, compatible with the extension functors. In particular their realization is the projection component in this statement. Conjugating by the chosen realization isomorphisms preserves its inverse. Together with steps 6 and 8 this exhausts all the coefficient stages of the datum. No finite reduction of a rational coefficient object is used.

proof_origin.place: Finite-stage comparison via the existing general ringed-topos exchange/tensor coherence theorem and the open tensor factor, followed by the existing adic and field theorems.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses clause (ii) to supply bounded constructible etale representatives of intrinsic finite-coefficient pro-etale inputs; the unit names comparison but has no origin-existence statement.
Step 1 descends the specified finite Tor intervals along the finite-ring comparison; constructible-origin equivalence alone does not give this test against all module sheaves.
Step 2 uses exact etale extension by zero to preserve boundedness of K_0; this is the open factor in the prescribed compact-support transport.
Step 2 replaces finite-Tor L_0 by a flat complex supported in its Tor interval to check boundedness of the second direct-image comparison input.
Step 2 uses clause (1) on the small etale site to make the bounded flat model K-flat before applying derived pullback; the unit has no K-flat criterion.
Steps 2 and 3 use preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes and the canonical monoidal derived pullback isomorphism, tools for the prescribed comparison route.
Step 2 turns separatedness of the proper compactification map into quasi-separatedness, verifying the canonical comparison mate hypothesis.

Step 3 applies the generic non-Cartesian ringed-topos square theorem to identify the actual counit-defined projection morphisms under comparison; this supplies the compatibility omitted in the unit sketch.
Step 3 uses exact comparison and the constant-ring identification to derive the pullback comparison termwise and compare open extension degreewise.
Step 3 uses the canonical commuting pullback isomorphism for the etale/pro-etale square; this implements the unit comparison-pullback sentence.
Step 3 uses the normalized canonical exchange mate and its invertibility for qcqs maps on both bounded-below inputs, rather than an unnamed isomorphism.
Step 3 identifies the etale and pro-etale open-extension factors, naturally in the inputs, as required by the unit compact-support transport.
Step 3 uses exact pro-etale extension by zero so the sheaf comparison induces the stated degreewise derived comparison.
Step 3 uses the canonical etale open tensor comparison and its sheaf-level normalization when comparing the compactification composites.
Step 3 uses the pro-etale open tensor comparison, the second factor of the compact-support projection composite.

Step 6 uses only its etale finite compact-support projection assertion for a separated finite-type morphism of arbitrary finite-type k-schemes; the named finite theorem unnecessarily assumes separated X,Y.
Step 6 records the finite etale projection theorem explicitly named by the unit on its separated-scheme domain; the general finite lemma supplies the same etale assertion on the full domain.
Step 7 uses bounded-below full faithfulness over a finite discrete ring to compare two origin witnesses and lift their inverse equations.
Step 8 uses the integral reconstruction and map-identification conclusion expressly delegated by the source proof, on its completed pro-etale coefficient system.
Step 9 uses invertibility and scalar-extension compatibility at rational and common finite stages, as expressly delegated by the unit.

lean.statement:
theorem sf_proetale_projection_formula
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f) :
    (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
      (n : ℕ)
      (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
      (L : proEtaleDerivedCategory Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
      (_hK : finiteTorConstructible l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) X K)
      (_hL : finiteTorConstructible l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) Y L)
      (_wK : SfProEtaleProjection.Origin X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) K)
      (_wL : SfProEtaleProjection.Origin Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) L),
      let P := Arrow.mk (((finiteRingCompactSupportProjection
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) c).app K).app L)
      ∃ (hS : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := proEtaleRingModules Y
          (proEtaleConstantRing Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))).plus P.left)
        (hT : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := proEtaleRingModules Y
          (proEtaleConstantRing Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))).plus P.right),
        IsIso (ObjectProperty.homMk P.hom :
          (⟨P.left, hS⟩ : DerivedCategory.Plus (proEtaleRingModules Y
            (proEtaleConstantRing Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))) ⟶
          (⟨P.right, hT⟩ : DerivedCategory.Plus (proEtaleRingModules Y
            (proEtaleConstantRing Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))))) ∧
    (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
      (aX : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l E X)
      (aZ : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l E c.Z)
      (aY : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l E Y)
      (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X)
      (L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y)
      (_hK : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X K.obj)
      (_hL : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E Y L.obj)
      (_wK : ∀ n : ℕ, SfProEtaleProjection.Origin X
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
          ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).obj K.obj))
      (_wL : ∀ n : ℕ, SfProEtaleProjection.Origin Y
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
          ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E Y n).obj L.obj)),
      IsIso (SfProEtaleProjection.integralMap l E D hl f c aX aZ aY K L)) ∧
    (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
      (aX : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l E X)
      (aZ : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l E c.Z)
      (aY : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l E Y)
      (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X)
      (L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y),
      IsIso ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l E Y).map
        (SfProEtaleProjection.integralMap l E D hl f c aX aZ aY K L))) ∧
    (∀ (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω]
      (F : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω)
      (aX : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l
        (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F) X)
      (aZ : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l
        (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F) c.Z)
      (aY : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel l
        (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F) Y)
      (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l
        (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F) X)
      (L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l
        (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F) Y),
      IsIso ((GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion (Y := Y) F).map
        ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l
          (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F) Y).map
            (SfProEtaleProjection.integralMap l
              (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω F)
                D hl f c aX aZ aY K L))))
lean.note: Reuses the already reviewed concrete four-stage theorem of sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale (this node blueprint.same_as).
